item.title: Sweden detains crew member of Russian 'shadow fleet' ship
item.description: Sweden has detained a crew member of a Russian 'shadow fleet' cargo ship suspected of transporting stolen Ukrainian grain, the Swedish coast guard said on Sunday.

item.title: NEW: The Local’s self-paced Swedish course
item.description: Due to popular demand The Local's self-paced online Swedish course for beginners is back, designed to make learning flexible and practical.

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Monday
item.description: There's a considerable risk of avalanches in the Swedish mountains and experts believe that the Iran war means Swedes can kiss any further interest rate cuts goodbye. More on that and the latest news here.

item.title: TELL US: What are your views on Sweden's deportation U-turn?
item.description: Sweden's government has struck an agreement with the Sweden Democrats to stop the deportation of young adults and of foreigners hit by the abolition of the track change law. We want to hear your views on this and whether it will affect you.

item.title: Sweden developing state-issued alternative to BankID
item.description: Both Swedish citizens and registered foreign residents of Sweden will be eligible for the planned government-issued electronic identification and verification service, which is currently being developed by the Swedish Police Agency.

item.title: Tackle this week’s Swedish crossword and word search puzzles
item.description: Have you been paying attention to the headlines? Do Saturday morning fika right with a cup of coffee and a mental workout. Every Saturday morning, we bring you a fresh crossword and word search that test your grasp of the Swedish zeitgeist.

item.title: Why April could be a good month for your Swedish finances
item.description: A tax rebate, cheaper food and even a potential pay rise ‒ April looks like it could be a good month financially for many people in Sweden.

item.title: Eight ways to save money on food and drink in Sweden
item.description: Sweden's Consumer Agency estimates a monthly food cost of 2,700 kronor for a single adult or 8,440 kronor for two adults and two children, but how can you lower that? Here are our top tips.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: skatt
item.description: Here's a Swedish word you can expect to hear a lot at this time of year as tax season gets under way.

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Tuesday
item.description: Right-wing extremist culture growing among young men, high grass fire risk in southern Sweden, Iran war expected to affect electricity prices and more news from Sweden on Tuesday.
